The largest strain the paper reports on the V₂O₅ film is an **in-plane tensile strain of about 1.6–1.66%**. It comes with an out-of-plane ("c"-direction) compressive strain of about **0.5%**. The authors summarize this as elastic prestrains of **"<2%"** on the V₂O₅ (acsnano-7b02404, p. 1/6243 abstract; p. 2/6244).

How these numbers were obtained:

- **Out-of-plane compression (measured):** The NiTi wire was stretched axially and the strain was kept in place by its shape-memory property (5% and 10% wire strains). X-ray diffraction of the (001) peak then showed an average out-of-plane compressive strain below 1%, reaching −0.5% in the strained states tested (p. 3/6245; p. 4/6246).
- **In-plane tension (estimated, not measured):** The authors assumed a Poisson ratio of 0.3, typical for metal oxides. On that basis they estimated "an in-plane tensile strain of 1.6% for an out of plane 'c' directional compressive strain of 0.5%" (p. 3/6245). Elsewhere they refer to it as "∼1.66% in-plane prestrain" (p. 5/6247).
- **Not the film's strain:** The 10% figure is the strain applied to the NiTi substrate. The authors stopped there to avoid the coating delaminating (p. 6/6248).
- **Simulations:** The DFT calculations modeled in-plane strains of up to ±2% on the V₂O₅ lattice (Figure 4d, p. 5/6247).

There is also a separate, built-in thermal strain from the mismatch in thermal expansion between the film and NiTi after annealing. It is larger in thinner films (Figure 1, p. 2/6244), but the text gives no specific maximum value for it.
